report:
Reviewed the complete current claim, all three ordinary implementation associations and all three ordinary annotated tests; there are no TODO/N/A entries or deferred requirements. Requirements are: select the entire content up to the defined boundary, remove surrounding whitespace, dedent enclosing .sage prose first while preserving relative internal whitespace and Markdown, and use the same content for saved inputs and generated anchor views.
Implementation: spec.rs parse_anchors closes active content at the next definition, headings, standalone explicit end comments, or source/prose-block end, with literal code/HTML handling. finish_anchor slices the full extent and trims only its exterior. load_workspace applies dedent to each .sage prose block before add_chapter_text; dedent removes the common leading spaces/tabs and retains relative indentation. review.rs inventory builds the Claim fragment directly from anchor.content through split-on-newline source_lines, so joining restores that content. Claim selection returns the same canonical content. book/anchors.rs claim passes anchor.content into the renderer for both individual pages and table disclosures and protects newlines for mdBook raw HTML. Captured browser renderer context confirms it consumes the whole supplied text. These three associated source files contain the essential selection, normalization, storage and shared-content behavior.
Tests: complete_claim_blocks_are_selected_but_unrelated_movement_is_not_stale asserts exact saved multiline text containing paragraphs, emphasis, a list, table and fenced example without outer whitespace or the explicit terminator; later-block mutations invalidate the review, while outside text changes and movement remain valid. sage_prose_rules_have_precise_spans_model_owners_and_cross_source_references asserts exact dedented content and exact review fragment text, including Unicode, Markdown, blank lines and retained four-space relative example indentation; independent prose blocks and entity/source spans are checked as well. Its updated lookup explicitly finds the Claim selector for crates.demo.nodes.value and unwraps its presence, preserving the prior substantive expected-string assertion. anchor_pages_and_disclosures_render_the_complete_reviewed_content asserts the review fragment equals its complete fixture claim, verifies every paragraph/list/table/code block in both rendered views, excludes outside commentary, checks view equality modulo relative URLs, and verifies a later Markdown pass retains protected HTML and does not leak example code. A truncation to the opening paragraph or removal of relative indentation would fail these exact assertions. Supplemental captured spec tests exercise other heading/next-definition/source-end and literal boundaries; those remain separate boundary-anchor coverage.
Additional captured context includes specification boundaries, review workflow, fixture helpers, the complete modified spec test file and rendering helper. This refresh compared all current initial fragments and metadata with the inputs previously consumed in this review thread. The sole change is an additional meta.reviews.source_representation test annotation on complete_claim_blocks_are_selected_but_unrelated_movement_is_not_stale; its complete executable test body and all other initial source fragments are unchanged. I re-captured and checked all previously used helper/specification context: those sources are unchanged too. The new annotation neither weakens nor changes the exact content assertion or staleness checks, so the requirement-to-evidence assessment above remains supported by current source. Source inspection is separate from execution: no tests were rerun for this annotation-only refresh. Earlier in this thread I personally ran the three targeted suites (21 review, 13 book and 30 spec tests passed), cargo fmt --check and cargo build. The coordinator now reports 331 sage-meta functional tests, 46 sage-stash tests and a workspace build passing; these current results are coordinator-reported, not my execution. No code or tests were modified by this reviewer. All current evidence is ordinary, every claim aspect remains covered, and no edits are requested.
